text: The Gerbrandy Tower (Dutch: Gerbrandytoren) is a radio tower located in IJsselstein, the Netherlands, and is also known as the Lopik tower due to its proximity to the town of Lopik. It was constructed in 1961 and is used for directional radio services, FM- and TV-broadcasting. The tower features a concrete structure 100 meters (328') high, upon which a guyed aerial mast is mounted. Its original total height was 382.5 metres (1,255 ft), but it was reduced to 375 metres (1,230 ft) in 1987. On August 2, 2007, its analog antenna was replaced with a digital one, reducing its height by another 9 metres (30 ft), bringing its current height to 366.8 metres (1,203 ft). This structure is a partially guyed tower, combining a lower free-standing concrete tower with an upper guyed mast. If counted as a tower, it is the tallest in Western Europe. A similar but smaller partially guyed tower exists in the Netherlands—the Zendstation Smilde radio tower—consisting of an 80-metre (260 ft) concrete tower with a 223.5-metre (733 ft) guyed mast. This tower collapsed after a fire on July 15, 2011, and was rebuilt starting in late 2011, completed in October 2012, with the replacement structure now standing at 303 metres (994 ft). The tower is named after Pieter Gerbrandy, who served as Prime Minister of the Netherlands during World War Two. Nearby, the KNMI-mast Cabauw is used for meteorological measurements, and the 196-metre (643 ft) high mediumwave transmitter Lopik was demolished on September 4, 2015. On July 15, 2011, a small fire occurred in the Gerbrandy Tower, prompting the immediate shutdown of all transmitters in the tower as a precaution, resulting in large parts of the Netherlands losing FM-radio and digital TV (DVB-T) reception, as the Smilde tower also caught fire and collapsed shortly after. Ownership of the tower is complex: the concrete main structure and the first three meters (10') of ground around the base are owned by Alticom, a company established in 2007 that acquired assets from KPN and was part of the European TDG Group; in June 2011, all Alticom shares were acquired by Infracapital, an infrastructure specialist of Prudential plc. The metal mast is owned by NOVEC, a subsidiary of TenneT. The ground surrounding the base, excluding the first three meters (10'), remains owned by KPN. Annually, from December 6 to January 6, the tower is decorated with 120 LED lamps attached to its 12 guy-wires, creating the appearance of a giant Christmas tree at night. In 1998, it was awarded by The Guinness Book of Records as the tallest Christmas tree in the world in a construction. The Mount Ingino Christmas Tree is also noted as the largest Christmas tree, though it is constructed on a hill slope.
